title: DevOps with SAP Business AI, How the Scope, Tooling & Mindset Change When You Adopt SAP BAIP
author: Rodrigo_Riveros
text:
Adopting SAP's Business AI Platform (BAIP) does not mean starting over on your DevOps practice. It means extending it — sometimes significantly. The conversations I have every day with customers going through BAIP onboarding repeatedly converge on the same realization: the teams that struggle the most are the ones who treat AI as a software deployment problem. The teams that thrive are the ones who understand that AI workloads introduce fundamentally different operational concerns. 
 This blog summarizes the key points I cover in my onboarding sessions. Whether you are a developer, a platform engineer, a solution architect, or a technical project manager, there is something here for you.

title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2609
author: kate_dowle
text:
SAP Asset Performance Management 2609 includes a feature you've been asking me about for a long time - a structured 5 Whys root cause analysis built directly into Reliability Cases. No more switching to a spreadsheet or whiteboard mid-investigation. This release also brings improvements in IoT-driven condition monitoring. 
 Before we start, I'd like to mention a couple of enablement materials you might find useful. 
 SAP partners and customers can join the SAP Asset Performance Management - Product Expert Training H2 2026 live session. Find details and register here . We're going to give a glimpse of the new AI agents coming out this year and the outlook for next year. 
 We've also updated our ongoing innovation overview (formerly Stay Current ), a curated guide to recent SAP APM innovations combining feature one-pagers with direct links to supporting enablement materials. The latest edition now covers releases 2509 - 2608. Download it here . 
 Now, let's take a closer look at SAP APM 2609. 
 Asset Reliability Engineering 
 5 Whys Root Cause Analysis in Reliability Cases 
 What if you could perform a structured root cause analysis directly inside SAP APM - without switching to a spreadsheet, a whiteboard, or a separate tool? 
 With this release, a dedicated 5 Whys root cause analysis section is now available inside Reliability Cases in SAP APM. 
 Challenge 
 When an asset failure occurs, reliability engineers need a structured methodology to trace the cause chain back to the origin. Until now, SAP APM had no built-in way to capture that analysis. Teams were working around the system - using external tools, documents, or informal notes - and the connection between root cause findings and follow-up actions was easily lost. 
 Solution 
 A dedicated 5 Whys analysis section is now part of the Reliability Case in SAP APM. Engineers can open a case, add cause chain levels one by one, and record the root cause with supporting context. The structured approach guides the team through the methodology while keeping all analysis and actions together in one place. 

 Because the analysis sits inside the Reliability Case, preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause. The completed analysis becomes part of the auditable case record - reusable for future investigations and visible to anyone who needs to understand how a failure was resolved. 
 5 Whys root cause analysis in SAP APM showing a completed cause chain for an unplanned gas turbine trip, with two converging fault branches traced from the problem through to root cause, and five corrective actions linked on the right. 
 Key Details 
 5 Whys analysis section available inside Reliability Cases 
 Engineers add cause chain levels sequentially and record the root cause with context 
 Preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause 
 Analysis becomes part of the auditable Reliability Case record 
 Business Value 
 This gives customers: 
 Root cause analysis completed entirely within SAP APM - no switching to external tools 
 Structured cause chains that are auditable and reusable for future failure investigations 
 Direct connection from root cause to preventive and corrective measures - nothing gets lost 
 Watch this video to see it in action 

 For more information, check this blog SAP Asset Performance Management Reliability Cases: A Practical Walkthrough Of Root Cause Analysis by @Pardhasaradhi_Reddy_Chelikam and see the SAP Help Portal Performing Root Cause Analysis . 
 Asset Health Monitoring 
 IoT Sensor Data Available in APM Within 15 Minutes 
 What if condition-based maintenance decisions were based on sensor readings from the last 15 minutes - not from two hours ago? 
 With this release, time series data ingested via the embedded IoT platform is now available in SAP APM rules and charts within 15 minutes of ingestion. 
 Challenge 
 Time series data sent from sensors into the embedded IoT platform could take up to two hours to appear in SAP APM. For teams using IoT data to drive condition-based maintenance rules and alerts, that delay meant rules fired late and the data behind a triggered alert was already stale. In fast-moving asset conditions, the gap between sensor reading and APM response was a real operational risk. 
 Solution 
 The data offloading interval and processing pipeline between the Embedded IoT platform and SAP APM has been significantly shortened. Time series data sent through standard HTTP and MQTT interfaces is now processed and made available in APM rules and the APM Chart within 15 minutes of ingestion - down from the previous baseline of up to 120 minutes. 

 No changes are required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations. Aggregate and analytics data sources are outside the scope of this improvement and may have longer processing times. 
 Key Details 
 Time series data via HTTP and MQTT available in APM within 15 minutes of ingestion 
 Applies to APM rules and the APM Chart 
 No changes required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations 
 Aggregate and analytics data sources are out of scope and may have longer processing times 
 Business Value 
 This gives customers: 
 Near-current sensor data in APM rules and charts - processing time reduced from up to 120 minutes to 15 minutes 
 Condition-based maintenance scenarios trigger faster, reducing response time to developing asset issues 
 Improved reliability of IoT-driven alerting with fresher data as the foundation 
 For more information, see Device Data Integration in SAP Asset Performance Management. . 
 Stay Informed and Get Involved 
 Check out the SAP Community for APM page - one stop shop for an overview of upcoming enablement sessions, content and learning opportunities for APM. Subscribe to get notified of updates. 
 Explore our latest APM blog posts here . 
 Find out what's up and coming in the SAP Road Map Explorer . 
 For the full feature documentation for 2609, visit the SAP Help Portal . 
 Check the latest update of the APM link collection . 
 See you for the next update! SAP Asset Performance Management

title: Electronic Invoicing in Germany with SAP Business ByDesign
author: ShaikShafi
text:
Electronic Invoicing in Germany with SAP Business ByDesign 
 SAP Business ByDesign supports compliance with the European E-Invoicing standard EN 16931 for outgoing customer invoices. 
 In accordance with Germany's regulatory requirements, e-invoicing will become mandatory for all businesses conducting B2B transactions effective January 1, 2027. 
 To comply with E-Invoicing, SAP Business ByDesign supports extensive output management and enables customers to generate XML output through custom XSLT transformations using the Transformation Repository framework. 
 This transformation feature supports Customer Invoices, Credit Memos and Down Payment Invoices. 
 The following blog describes how to configure the transformation settings to enable the system to send an E-Invoice. 
 E-Invoicing with SAP Business ByDesign 
 Disclaimer: 
 This solution is provided as a reference example to demonstrate the transformation capabilities available in SAP Business ByDesign. Customers are responsible for validating and adapting the output to meet their legal and business requirements. 
 As the template is only an example it might be necessary to adapt the template to individual customer requirements. 
 Attached is the sample XSLT template which would generate XRechnung UBL 3.0.1 compliant XML. 
 IMPORTANT : You must change the file type to .xslt before you can use it. 
 Apart from XSLT transformation feature, SAP Business ByDesign offer another option to customers to exchange their electronic invoices and credit memos through the Peppol E-Delivery network. 
 SAP Business ByDesign can exchange electronic invoices and credit memos through the Peppol network using Universal Business Language (UBL) documents that comply with the XRechnung format ( XRechnung UBL Invoice V3.0 and XRechnung UBL CreditNote V3.0). This capability is provided by SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. 
 Please check the following blog for more information. 
 Integrating SAP Business ByDesign to Peppol Networ... - SAP Community . 
 Relevant KBA's: 
 KBA 3016103 - Is ZUGFeERD supported in Business By Design? 
 KBA 2768238 - How to Perform E-Invoicing in SAP Business ByDesign

title: Who Sets the Pace of AI?
author: Verena
text:
AI is moving at incredible speed. But who should set the pace? 
 One insight really stayed with me after AIDAQ 2026: 
 AI is advancing faster than many organizations can make decisions about how to use it responsibly. 
 Interestingly, there is often a clear gap between our private and professional use of AI. 
 At home, many of us use AI naturally: 
 Writing and improving texts 
 Planning trips 
 Researching topics 
 Exploring ideas and possibilities 
 At work, things look different. We assess risks, review compliance requirements, run pilots, and evaluate impact before scaling. 
 And that's a good thing. 
 In business, we are responsible for data, processes, customers, and employees. The decisions we make today will have long-term consequences. 
 That is why shaping the future of AI requires more than speed. It requires diverse perspectives, responsible leadership, and human oversight. 
 Europe may not need to build the fastest AI. 
 But perhaps we can build the most trustworthy AI. 
 AI that is trained with diverse perspectives. AI that is fair and inclusive. AI that keeps humans in control. 
 This was one of the key topics we discussed during the panel "Shaping the AI Future" at AIDAQ 2026. 
 Discussion Question 
 How is your organization balancing speed of AI adoption with responsibility, governance, and trust ? 
 Where do you see the biggest challenge today: moving fast enough or ensuring AI is implemented responsibly? 
 I would love to hear your experiences and perspectives from across the SAP community.

title: Observing an issue with parallel multicast in SAP Integration Suite
author: S0016728925
text:
Dear Experts, 
 I have a very simple scenario of receiving a XML message from sender via HTTPs and using Parallel multicast, I intend to send the data to almost 12 different downstream systems. Each multicast path is then having router validation (XPATH). 
 The sample Data that I trigger should go to 10 systems (based on condition validation). 
 When I trigger a data to the iFlow in 'Info' mode --> the message is processed only to 1 downstream system. 
 When I trigger the same data in 'Trace' mode --> the message is processed to 8 downstream system. 
 With trace enabled, I checked the message steps and noticed that 2 multicast branches were not even triggered at all . This issue is observed in our UAT tenant. But the same flow worked correctly in lower Dev Tenant. 
 Can anyone tell me why this happens? 
 Is there any limit to Parallel multicast branch count? 
 If any receiver is down, will parallel multicast process get impacted? Ideally - it should trigger all branches and send data to all systems. 
 Could it be platform issue? There are multiple other iFlows that are using Parallel multicast (and no issues have been reported) 
 Does enabling trace change the way SAP IS processes a message? Never seen this so far.
